verification_report.summary: The full proof passes sequential verification under the explicitly stated real-polyhedral definitions. The one-vertex lemma correctly characterizes convexity by raywise convexity and all nonnegative balancing relations, with the stated weighted Laplacian mass. Strictly positive balancing weights justify the dimension formula. In the rank-one case, the local raising perturbations preserve convexity, the obstacle bound, and admissible growth, forcing every positive atom into the contact set. For higher-dimensional relation cones, the extreme-ray construction gives the exact claimed envelope and a strictly negative orthogonality integral. The bounded-reference-shift identity and the nonsaturated tripod example are correct. For graphs, the slope inequalities remain valid after subdivision, and the vertex perturbation works along bounded edges and around cycles; the valence-at-most-three corollary follows from the distinct outgoing directions. The cited results were checked against [BMPS26](https://arxiv.org/html/2603.08664v1): the real-affine envelope argument, primitive-coordinate Laplacian normalization, and local convexity characterization support their uses here. The integral-slope warning is valid, and no unproved graph converse is asserted.
